Hoskinson: Cardano Not Done Yet

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (478 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: U

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson, there is plenty more to come for Cardano, as the blockchain's privacy-preserving sister chain, Midnight, reaches a huge milestone as its ecosystem continues to expand.
  • Charles Hoskinson made sure to clear up misunderstandings about whether he thought the work on Cardano was done.
  • Industry observers note that "I never once said Cardano is finished," Hoskinson said in a Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson, there is plenty more to come for Cardano, as the blockchain's privacy-preserving sister chain, Midnight, reaches a huge milestone as its ecosystem continues to expand.

Charles Hoskinson made sure to clear up misunderstandings about whether he thought the work on Cardano was done.

Industry observers note that "I never once said Cardano is finished," Hoskinson said in a Nov. 15 post on X.

The comments came after he talked about the completion of Cardano's original roadmap, which raised some questions about his role in the blockchain's future.

He also called out the CEO of the Cardano Foundation, Frederik Gregaard, for not mentioning the Midnight chain when discussing everything the network has accomplished.

In his latest video, uploaded on Nov. 17, Hoskinson celebrated the fact that Midnight had just brought on board its first UK-based banking partner, Monument Bank.

Monument Bank is the first UK bank to offer interest-bearing tokenized retail deposits on a public blockchain, according to an announcement from the Midnight Foundation.

Up to £250 million in customer deposits will be added to Midnight in the first phase, and each tokenized deposit will be backed 1:1 by sterling cash held at the bank.

Monument Bank customers can now earn a fixed 5.2% annual equivalent rate on deposits for 12 months, all without having to deal with cryptocurrencies directly.

Hoskinson was very excited about the scale of the initiative, comparing the planned amount of deposits with the current decentralized finance ecosystem on Cardano.

"It's five times the TVL of Cardano," he stated.

The £250 million is the planned initial size of the banking product, not a verified figure for how much is currently deposited on Midnight.

Hoskinson called this one of the most crucial milestones in his career.

"This is just one of the many things to come, but I think it's one of the most significant things of at least my career," he said.

He added that the team behind Midnight had moved the originally scheduled hard fork from December to November to accommodate the technical needs of Monument Bank.

Despite the milestone, Hoskinson emphasized that it's only the first step in a much larger mission: bringing traditional financial assets onto Midnight.

In a recent development, "This mission is not done if these assets are just strictly staying on Midnight. Needs to be expanded to Web3. But inherit from Midnight in terms of safety, security, privacy, simplicity," he stated.

Hoskinson thinks the main barrier to cryptocurrency adoption is the lack of trust among consumers. He believes that simplifying the user experience without compromising regulatory requirements will allow billions of people to join the blockchain economy.

Industry observers note that hoskinson also shared that there's a significant event coming up for the Midnight Foundation on Dec. 15. Developers will showcase future products and technological advancements scheduled for 2027.

Recent findings suggest that XRP is close to a $61 billion market cap, but its $0.9763 price still needs a real catalyst to recover. XRP's market capitalization is on the verge of breaking the $60 billion barrier after the massive drop. According to some aggregators, the price has already crossed the mark, while CoinMarketCap still shows $61 billion.

The state of the market is very far from bullish: there's a good chance we won't see a proper, full-blown recovery sooner than next year, especially after the $6.1 billion wipeout on the cryptocurrency market.

However, XRP has multiple foundational advantages over competitors, such as stronger institutional backing and the use of its network for overseas transactions.

According to recent reports, XRP is trading at $0.9763 after dipping to around $0.89 during the drop, and it is below $1 for the first time since mid-August. RSI touched the oversold zone near 30 and has bounced slightly since. The nearest moving average sits around $1.13, while the longest one is above $1.30.

The asset has reached the area of the previous recovery, which will most likely push the market to the limit, as most traders want to break even on their positions rather than keep losing money. A potentially better time to buy XRP could be tied to the overall market recovery, hence the occurrence of a better market catalyst, which doesn't exist at this point.

The confirmation of a market recovery would only come if we witness specific signs of a bull run on larger-cap altcoins: higher highs and constant inflows into institutional products like ETFs.

Sources indicate that dogecoin lost more than 30% of its value in the breakdown that started on October 8. It destroyed all the gains Dogecoin had made in the past: September's peak is gone, and the price dropped to the lowest level in 4 years. However, it's not all doom and gloom.

DOGE is trading at $0.05963, which is around 43% lower than the September peak near $0.105. Dogecoin has been slowly tumbling for weeks, showing a continuous bearish dynamic, and it is now below all the moving averages. Volume spiked during the drop and has faded over the last two days.

According to multiple long-term momentum indicators, Dogecoin is extremely oversold. RSI and MVRV both suggest a bounce coming in the foreseeable future. While it's not guaranteed, obviously, there is potential. Most altcoins didn't see any spikes in selling because they were already oversold. The $0.068 area, where Dogecoin held in July and August, is already lost.

It has been revealed that the cryptocurrency market moves in cycles, and the recent risk-on cycle in the global economy was exclusive to AI and tech stocks. The crypto market, on the other hand, missed out on it, and with no substantial gains and increased pressure in November, we got the double hit that destroyed hopes for a quick recovery.

Crypto might benefit from a transitional period on the market, even though it's not guaranteed by any means, as both risk tolerance and available funds are running dry.

Solana has almost reached the threshold of $43 billion market capitalization, according to data from CoinMarketCap. The asset is slowly moving back into the bullish zone after it joined other altcoins in a massive price drop. That's around 70% of XRP's $61 billion.

Solana mostly followed the general uptrend but tumbled quickly due to the general reversal of the cryptocurrency market. SOL is trading at $73.75, down around 41% from the late September peak near $125. It dipped to approximately $67.5 during the drop and has bounced for two days, with RSI turning up from the oversold zone.

Industry observers note that every moving average on the chart sits above the price, with the nearest one around $87. Investors aren't buying en masse, but there is some accumulation, which could be tied to automated market making.

The correction on Solana is no different from other assets, and, unfortunately, SOL didn't show any additional resilience on the market.

From a price development perspective, the only positive outcome we are witnessing is the bounce from the August low zone, which might become support at some point, though that is not happening yet.

The dip below $70, which was the point of reversal back in August, is where some buy orders might be concentrated.

At the moment, Solana is stuck in the approximately $70-$75 price range, and it seems unlikely to break out until it gets back to the moving averages at around $94-$96.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Tuesday, Zcash price highlighted a massive rally, rising more than 10%.

At press time, ZEC is reading near $961. The recovery follows a sharp a correction that pushed ZEC toward $860 over the weekend.

Despite the rebound, the ZEC remains under pressure from institutional fund withdrawals.

One of the most important developments is a Zcash Community Grants (ZCG) vote running from November 16 to November 30.

Community members are considering proposals to change how the grants treasury is managed, including a proposal to transfer 50,000 ZEC into the Network Sustainability Mechanism.

In a recent development, zcash gained 7.69% on November 4, rising on high expectations surrounding NU7. The upgrade introduces several changes to the network's transaction processing and reward structure.

As the upgrade went live on November 5, the target block interval went from 75 seconds to 25 seconds. According to the project’s statement, the change makes private payments confirm three times faster.

Recent findings suggest that ZEC recently tested the $860 area before recovering. This level is crucial because derivatives data previously identified a concentration of leveraged long positions around it.

If Zcash returns to that zone, forced liquidations could amplify volatility. $950 is an initial recovery level, followed by the psychological resistance around $1,000.

However, break below $860 could expose ZEC to selling pressure and further decline.

New York’s Luxury Rental Market Sees Influx of Cash from AI Boom

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The artificial intelligence boom has expanded from the rolling hills of San Francisco and Silicon Valley to the busy streets of Newly introduced York City, where an already tight luxury market is feeling the impact.
  • The AI wealth boom was in the spotlight this week, following Anthropic’s highly anticipated IPO and jaw dropping $1.494 trillion valuation.
  • There are more than 2,000 AI companies operating in New York City, according to the city’s Economic Development Corporation, and AI companies signed leases for about 1.5 million square feet in just the first six months of 2026, the Brooklyn Daily Eagle reported.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The artificial intelligence boom has expanded from the rolling hills of San Francisco and Silicon Valley to the busy streets of Newly introduced York City, where an already tight luxury market is feeling the impact.

The AI wealth boom was in the spotlight this week, following Anthropic’s highly anticipated IPO and jaw dropping $1.494 trillion valuation. With the tech constantly growing and producing newly minted millionaires, the impacts of deep-pocketed AI professionals entering the New York real estate market are just beginning to be felt, agents there say.

There are more than 2,000 AI companies operating in New York City, according to the city’s Economic Development Corporation, and AI companies signed leases for about 1.5 million square feet in just the first six months of 2026, the Brooklyn Daily Eagle reported.

Major AI frontrunners like Anthropic, Palantir, OpenAI, and EliseAI have opened offices in Upcoming York, contributing to the thriving commercial real estate market.

“It’s been pretty unbelievable, what’s happening in the public sphere of the AI business. We’re seeing a ton of AI leasing activity on the ground in Latest York,” Evan Kleinberg, co-founder of Cornelia Street Partners, a boutique commercial real estate firm, told Realtor.com. “And it’s been happening so fast, it’s almost representative of the technology itself. The companies hire immediately and they need space yesterday.”.

While Kleinberg has been keeping eyes on the AI industry for the past couple of years, his brokerage worked with its first AI specific firm about 12 months ago, at the end of 2025. Since then, the brokerage has secured leases for five companies developing proprietary AI models.

There are a number of reasons Kleinberg sees AI companies expanding east and planting roots in Latest York. The city has fully rebounded from the pandemic and has an attractive lifestyle that draws many young professionals. Plus, companies see the benefit of being close to their portfolio businesses.

“Ultimately, if your goal is to raise money from Goldman Sachs or JP Morgan or one of the major private equity groups like Apollo, they’re all here,” Kleinberg explained. “So wanting to get close to them is an underlying reason to move.”.

With these newly introduced offices comes a hoard of young, newly wealthy professionals who are looking to build a home in New York, many of whom are stepping into an already fiercely competitive luxury real estate market.

“Wall Street has historically been a major driver of Manhattan luxury real estate, and now we’re really starting to see the effects of AI. It’s becoming an important engine for wealth creation and housing demand,” Michelle Griffith, a residential real estate agent in Newly introduced York City, told Realtor.com. “Right now in Manhattan, we are already in a very tight rental market. Even for the last year, rents are up anywhere from 10% to 20% in Manhattan, especially for these luxury properties.”.

According to recent reports, as of November, the median sold price of a home in Manhattan is $1,150,000, a 15% year over year increase. Some Manhattan neighborhoods have had more extreme changes.

Sources indicate that the Lower East Side, for example, saw the median sale price jump 28% year over year to $1,435,000. Rent in the Lower East Side also increased 11% year over year, for a median of $5,947 per month.

Industry observers note that the Latest York City luxury residential landscape is no stranger to competition, with deep pocketed masses vying for a severely limited inventory of spaces. With the flood of AI professionals, another layer of people has been added to the market.

Griffith recalled a recent listing at 50 Gramercy Park North, which had historically rented for $30,000. While a rental like this, which is in the higher end of the market, would previously take 30 to 60 days to identify a tenant, the listing had eight rental bids after 48 hours on the market, with half above asking.

Most workers are determined to live close to work, making it especially challenging to secure an apartment in these highly sought after neighborhoods.

OpenAI’s 90,000-square-foot Fresh York office is located in the Puck Building, which sits on the boarder of SoHo and Nolita in Manhattan.

Anthropic’s Latest York hub takes up the entirety of a 16-story building at 330 Hudson Street in the Hudson Square neighborhood of Lower Manhattan.

“The offices are in fantastic locations, so it’s easy to find great housing within walking distance,” mentioned Griffith. “The challenge is finding that apartment because there is very, very limited inventory because those neighborhoods were already popular and in demand.”.

For luxury agents, the challenge is no longer finding tenants with the money to rent high priced rentals, its finding the rentals for deep pocketed tenants.

Industry observers note that when Griffith began in real estate 15 years ago, an apartment for $100,000 per month might be the biggest rental of the year. Now, rentals for $80,000 to even $150,000 are common and moving quickly, she shared.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following multiple technical outages at major U.S. banks that left thousands of people unable to access banking services or make transactions, Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley has urged Americans to keep some of their funds in crypto or stablecoins as a backup plan.

In a recent X post, Horsley pointed to the weaknesses of traditional financial systems, especially in the context of the world's growing reliance on technology.

"Rolling bank outages in the AI era," he said.

"Consider having some stablecoins or crypto just in case.".

Large U.S. financial institutions such as JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and Wells Fargo experienced widespread complaints about technical outages on Nov. 16.

Customers mentioned they were having trouble logging into their online accounts, viewing their balances and conducting transactions.

It has been revealed that according to Fox News, the incident affected some of the biggest banking names in the U.S. Thousands of people reported the matter via the outage-tracking platform Downdetector.

Industry observers note that zelle, a popular payment service that people use in the U.S. to transfer funds between bank accounts, was also reportedly affected.

In a recent development, as of the evening of Nov. 16, Chase had fixed the technical problem, according to the bank. It said transactions were back to normal.

Recent findings suggest that the outage reports initially pointed to multiple banking systems going down at the same time. But further investigation revealed that problems at Chase spilled over into transactions with other banks. However, the Zelle app itself continued to work.

Stablecoins such as USDT and USDC aim to track the value of the U.S. dollar as closely as possible. They can be an option for those looking to hold digital funds without the extreme price fluctuations of crypto assets like Bitcoin.

For instance, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, participants in blockchain networks can transfer dollar-based stablecoins 24/7. However, cashing them out into traditional money may still require access to traditional financial institutions.

AI deals shrink to as little as 30 days as the data layer sets the pace

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that the storage industry’s longtime performance specialist sees that shift as its opening.
  • Sources indicate that “When you look at the data layer, performance in the data layer drives value.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 14:27 EST / NOVEMBER 20 2026.

It has been revealed that artificial intelligence has turned data infrastructure from a back-office purchase into the bottleneck that decides how fast GPUs pay off. As hyperscalers, neoclouds and enterprises race to expand their data layers, the way that infrastructure gets bought is changing just as fast.

Industry observers note that the storage industry’s longtime performance specialist sees that shift as its opening. DataDirect Networks Inc. built its reputation on scale and speed, and those traits now carry more weight in AI infrastructure, according to Kevin Delane (pictured), president and chief revenue officer of DDN.

Sources indicate that “When you look at the data layer, performance in the data layer drives value. So yes, it has to be simple, it has to be reliable. Those are table stakes, but performance drives business value,” Delane stated.

Delane spoke with theCUBE Research’s Rebecca Knight and John Furrier at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how AI infrastructure sales cycles have grown more complex and faster, DDN’s tighter ecosystem work with partners such as Nvidia Corp. and Super Micro Computer Inc., and the firm’s hiring for a direct, results-driven culture. (* Disclosure below.).

The way companies buy AI infrastructure has changed along with the technology. Deals at neocloud providers no longer go to a single enterprise buyer. They now involve the off-taker renting the capacity, the cloud operator and the integration software layer, Delane explained. Timelines have shrunk just as sharply, from six months to a year for a traditional enterprise sale to as little as 30 days.

“The sales cycle is more complex for sure. The speed is insane,” Delane mentioned. “Sometimes these things are 30 days and you have to be ready to turn things around and really work with your customers and partners quickly.”.

Industry observers note that DDN is answering with tighter ecosystem work. Its decade-long partnership with Nvidia anchors the strategy, and joint offerings with Super Micro, such as the Enterprise AI HyperPOD, aim to replace a data center buildout with a ready-to-run AI stack. At SC26, DDN also introduced software-defined EXAScaler deployment to give enterprise AI customers more choice of hardware.

“It takes the complexity out of it, allows an enterprise to set up an AI pod within 3 hours,” Delane remarked.

The performance case holds up in the public cloud too. On Google LLC’s Google Cloud, customers using DDN’s Managed Lustre service saw 70% better training performance and a 40% gain in overall GPU efficiency, Delane noted.

Industry observers note that DDN is growing threefold this year while adding only a few salespeople, leaning its hiring toward technical and implementation staff who can get customers up and running faster. Delane looks for grit and a fit with a direct, results-driven culture.

“If people can fit that culture, want to come in, want to grow this manufacturer to multiple billions, we have a place for them,” Delane stated.

October Marks the First Month in 3 Years With a Decline in U.S. Home-Sale Prices

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1042 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Redfin

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that for three years, U.S.
  • Recent findings suggest that the median home-sale price declined 0.4% year over year to $388,634 in October.
  • With the total number of homes for sale at its highest level since early 2020 and demand cooling, homebuyers’ negotiating power keeps increasing–and that’s finally showing up in sale prices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that for three years, U.S. home-sale prices rose from a year earlier every single month, even as mortgage rates climbed and would-be buyers pulled back. That streak has ended.

Recent findings suggest that the median home-sale price declined 0.4% year over year to $388,634 in October. That’s  the first decline since May 2023 and a sharp slowdown from the 2.5% gain just two months earlier. With Americans’ wages growing about 4% year over year, even a slight dip in prices can improve affordability. Sale prices have risen nearly every single month for the last 13 years; the only exception was a handful of months in 2023.

With the total number of homes for sale at its highest level since early 2020 and demand cooling, homebuyers’ negotiating power keeps increasing–and that’s finally showing up in sale prices.

According to recent reports, home-sale prices fell nationwide, but they rose in more than half of the 50 most populous U.S. metro areas. San Francisco led the nation by a wide margin, with the median sale price rising 16.8% year over year. That’s the biggest increase since 2018. Next comes Fresh Brunswick, NJ, with a 7.7% gain. Two other NYC-area metros also had price increases ranking in the top six; the median sale price rose 4.4% in both New York City and Nassau County.

In San Francisco, AI wealth is fueling competition for scarce inventory; active listings were down 7% from a year earlier. In the Upcoming York City area, years of limited homebuilding have left buyers competing for relatively few homes in a region with a strong job market.

Industry observers note that home-sale prices fell most in Austin, TX, where they declined 6.5% year over year. It’s followed by Seattle (-5.1%) and Nashville, TN (-4.9%). Austin and Nashville are among the biggest buyer’s markets in the U.S., and Seattle’s shaky tech job market is curbing demand.

Industry observers note that national sale prices are losing steam because fewer Americans can afford to buy a home. U.S. pending home sales fell 3.6% from a month earlier in October on a seasonally adjusted basis to their lowest level since 2013, with the exception of April 2020.

This is a real-time indicator of the state of the housing market; fewer homes went under contract in October largely because mortgage rates averaged 7.33%, a three-year high and up from 6.86% the month before.

Industry observers note that all figures in this report are seasonally adjusted, with the exception of median sale price data and mortgage rate data. See a more detailed methodology here and view an interactive dashboard here.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s a buyer’s market, but not many people can afford to buy,” stated Chen Zhao, Redfin’s head of economics. “That could start to shift a bit, now that sale prices are closer to reflecting the shape of the market. House hunters in most of the country should know that the price they see on a listing may very well be a starting point; they should try offering below the asking price, and negotiating for closing costs, repairs and maybe even mortgage-rate buydowns. If you can’t get the price or monthly payment you want on one house, move on to the next one–with a big pool of inventory sitting on the market, buyers can afford to be picky.”.

It has been revealed that pending home sales declined in all of the most populous U.S. metros. That’s the second month in a row that has happened; before September, the last time was three years earlier.

The biggest declines were in Seattle and San Diego, both places where pending sales fell more than 20% year over year. Those West Coast metros are some of the priciest in the U.S., so 7%-plus mortgages hit house hunters’ monthly payments there hard. In Seattle, an uncertain local job market is also curbing demand.

Closed home sales fell to their lowest level in nearly 3 years. They declined 2.1% month over month in October to their lowest level since December 2023; before that, the last time sales dropped that low was 2014. Many of the deals that closed last month went under contract in August and September, when rates were already climbing and economic uncertainty was deterring a lot of house hunters.

With homebuying demand falling, supply is building. The total number of homes for sale rose 0.9% from September to its highest level since early 2020; that’s the biggest monthly gain since May 2025.

More supply gives buyers more homes to choose from and more leverage:.

Industry observers note that “Buyers are nervous about rates, the economy, and everything they’re seeing in the news– so they need the house and the price to line up perfectly before they’ll make an offer,” said Callie Kimmel, a Redfin Premier agent in Philadelphia. “I’m advising sellers to price just below current market value from day one–and not comps from six months ago, but homes that are listed right now. Otherwise, the home is likely to end up sitting on the market for a bit and selling for less than they hoped. There are a few exceptions: Move-in ready homes in the most desirable neighborhoods are still competitive; in those cases, sellers have the upper hand.”.

Industry observers note that while total housing supply is growing, fewer sellers are adding newly introduced inventory to the pool. New listings of homes for sale fell 1% month over month to the lowest level in more than two years. Would-be sellers are pulling back as homebuying demand slows and sale prices lose steam.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bitcoin mining giant MARA Holdings, formerly known as Marathon Digital, continues to offload its Bitcoin holdings, with another multimillion-dollar transfer spotted as the organization's selling spree shows no signs of slowing down.
  • According to blockchain analytics platform Lookonchain, MARA transferred another 366 BTC, worth approximately $23.33 million, from its wallets on Nov.
  • The latest transaction follows a series of substantial Bitcoin sales by the mining organization throughout 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin mining giant MARA Holdings, formerly known as Marathon Digital, continues to offload its Bitcoin holdings, with another multimillion-dollar transfer spotted as the organization's selling spree shows no signs of slowing down.

According to blockchain analytics platform Lookonchain, MARA transferred another 366 BTC, worth approximately $23.33 million, from its wallets on Nov. 18.

The latest transaction follows a series of substantial Bitcoin sales by the mining organization throughout 2026.

Lookonchain estimates that MARA has already sold a staggering 40,581 BTC this year, generating approximately $3.03 billion at an average selling price of $74,446 per coin.

However, it remains unclear whether the latest 366 BTC transfer represents another completed sale or an internal movement of funds.

MARA's aggressive selling strategy is confirmed by its latest quarterly financial disclosures.

Industry observers note that according to its Nov. 9 SEC filing, the company sold approximately 26,984 BTC for $1.9 billion during the first nine months of 2026.

Following the end of September, MARA liquidated another 13,597 BTC at an average price of approximately $81,039, raising an additional $1.1 billion.

These transactions bring its total disclosed Bitcoin sales to 40,581 BTC.

Notably, the manufacturer used $750 million from its latest sales to fully repay Bitcoin-backed loans, releasing 17,477 BTC previously pledged as collateral.

Interestingly, MARA has explicitly signaled that it intends to continue selling Bitcoin as part of a broader shift in its corporate strategy.

However, it began allowing sales of newly mined Bitcoin in 2025 before expanding the policy in 2026 to include coins already held on its balance sheet.

In its latest shareholder letter, MARA remarked it prepares to continue monetizing Bitcoin to strengthen its financial flexibility.

The company specifically identified artificial intelligence infrastructure, upcoming convertible debt obligations and potential share repurchases as reasons for building up cash reserves.

The selling comes as MARA faces considerable pressure on its core mining business.

Third-quarter revenue declined 35% year over year to $164.2 million, compared to $252.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025.

#110643. Just 3 Major U.S. Metros Are Seller’s Markets–the Fewest Since the Pandemic Freeze

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1339 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Redfin ↗ Open Full Page

Just 3 Major U.S. Metros Are Seller’s Markets–the Fewest Since the Pandemic Freeze

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1339 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Redfin

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, just three of the 50 most populous U.S.
  • According to recent reports, nassau County, NY was the number-one seller’s market, with 24.7% fewer sellers than buyers.
  • It has been revealed that all three seller’s markets became less strong seller’s markets in October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, just three of the 50 most populous U.S. metro areas were seller’s markets in October. That’s tied for the fewest in records dating back to 2016, matching April 2020, when the pandemic froze the housing market.

According to recent reports, nassau County, NY was the number-one seller’s market, with 24.7% fewer sellers than buyers. The other seller’s markets were Newark, NJ (-14.3%) and Montgomery County, PA (-12.1%).

It has been revealed that all three seller’s markets became less strong seller’s markets in October. In Nassau County, there were 28.3% fewer sellers than buyers in September, a bigger gap than October’s 24.7%. Newark’s gap shrunk from 17.6% to 14.3%, and Montgomery County’s shrunk from 20.1% to 12.1%. Milwaukee, which was a seller’s market in September, is now balanced, meaning it doesn’t favor sellers or buyers.

Recent findings suggest that the seller’s markets are places where limited homebuilding has kept housing supply tight. In the greater New York City area, combine that with strong demand for homes near a major job center, and buyers are competing for homes. Home-sale prices rose an average of 3.3% year over year across the three seller’s markets in October. That’s compared with a 0.3% uptick across all of the buyer’s markets, a sign that in seller’s markets, competition among buyers is pushing up home prices.

Industry observers note that “Buyers looking in these pockets of the Northeast should be prepared for a very different experience than buyers elsewhere in the country,” noted Redfin Senior Economist Asad Khan. “They may have less room to negotiate, especially on desirable, move-in-ready homes, and could face multiple-offer situations. If you’re shopping in one of these markets, it’s especially important to know your budget, be ready to act when the right home comes along and avoid getting swept up in a bidding war.”.

Seller’s markets are the exception to a national picture that heavily favors buyers.

Nationwide, homebuyers have more negotiating power than at any point in Redfin’s records. There were an estimated 70.5% more home sellers than buyers in the U.S. housing market in October, the biggest gap in records dating back to 2013.

Industry observers note that that marks the sixth record-breaking month in a row, and the margin is up from 65.6% in September. The Sun Belt is driving the extreme buyer’s market nationwide, led by huge seller surpluses in Miami, Nashville, TN and Las Vegas.

When sellers outnumber buyers, buyers typically have more negotiating power because they have options. That’s why a market with a lot more sellers than buyers is considered a buyer’s market. We define a market where there are over 10% more sellers than buyers as a buyer’s market and a market where there are over 10% fewer sellers than buyers as a seller’s market. A market where the gap is plus or minus 10% is considered a balanced market.

Recent findings suggest that we estimated the number of buyers using proprietary Redfin data on the typical time from a buyer’s first tour to close of purchase, and MLS data on active listings and pending sales. The estimated number of sellers in the market is simply the number of active listings in the MLS. These estimates are seasonally adjusted and subject to revision. See a more detailed methodology here and view an interactive dashboard here.

It’s only a buyer’s market for people who can afford to buy. High housing costs and economic jitters have pushed many would-be homebuyers to back off in recent years, creating the imbalance between buyers and sellers we see today.

According to recent reports, “A buyer-friendly market can help make homeownership a little more attainable, even if it doesn’t solve the affordability challenges that have kept many people on the sidelines,” Khan said. “Sellers are increasingly competing for buyers’ attention, which can translate into price reductions, concessions and other savings. First-time buyers don’t have equity from a previous home to put toward a purchase, which makes saving for a down payment a substantial hurdle–but they also don’t have to sell a home before they can buy or give up a low mortgage rate. With a historic buyer’s market and home prices that are finally ticking down after three years of increases, first-time buyers who have been waiting–and can afford today’s costs–may have an opportunity to make a move.”.

The gap between buyers and sellers widened in October because would-be buyers retreated, while sellers continued listing their homes, albeit at a sluggish pace.

There were an estimated 895,752 homebuyers in the market nationwide in October, the lowest level in records dating back to 2013. That’s down 2% from a month earlier, the sixth straight monthly decline. Mortgage rates averaged 7.33% in October, up from 6.86% in September, which priced out more would-be buyers.

Industry observers note that on the flip side, there were an estimated 1,526,984 home sellers in the market, the most since March 2020. That’s up 0.9% month over month.

The number of homes on the market is piling up because many homes are lingering on the market for months without going under contract. Each month, more upcoming listings are adding to the major pool of supply.

Recent findings suggest that some homeowners keep listing their houses despite falling demand because many have given up on waiting for lower rates. They may want to sell now because they’re worried prices could decline, and some need to move for a new job, a growing family, or another life change. But many homeowners who don’t need to move have substantial equity and little pressure to sell, so they may hold off on listing.

Recent findings suggest that over 80% of U.S. metro areas, 41 of the 50 Redfin analyzed, are buyer’s markets. That matches September’s record.

For the third month in a row, Miami and Nashville have the biggest surpluses of sellers over buyers. Miami had 195.8% more sellers than buyers in October, and Nashville had 159.5% more. Las Vegas (149.9%) was third on the list. In the top 13 buyer’s markets, there were more than twice as many sellers as buyers in October. Nearly all are in the Sun Belt; four are in Texas and four are in Florida.

The Sun Belt, particularly Texas and Florida, is home to some of the nation’s biggest buyer’s markets, partly because of robust homebuilding. Builders are continuing to add newly introduced homes even as demand cools, swelling inventory and giving buyers more options and negotiating power.

In a recent development, demand has cooled largely because rising mortgage rates and stubbornly high home prices are pricing buyers out. In Florida, rising HOA and homeowners insurance costs are exacerbating the affordability squeeze.

Six metros were “balanced” in October, neither buyer’s nor seller’s markets: Chicago (8.1% more sellers than buyers), Boston (7.5%), Providence, RI (7.5%), New Brunswick, NJ (5.6%), Milwaukee (0.6% fewer sellers than buyers) and San Francisco (6.9% fewer).

The surplus of home sellers over buyers grew month over month in 34 of the 41 buyer’s markets in October.

The surplus increased most in Miami, which also has the biggest surplus of sellers over buyers; there were 195.8% more sellers than buyers in October, up from 160.5% the month before. The next-biggest monthly increases were in Las Vegas, where there were 149.9% more sellers than buyers, up from 122.8%, and Nashville (159.5%, up from 134.3%).

House hunters lost negotiating power in seven buyer’s markets. The surplus of sellers over buyers fell from September to October in Fort Worth, TX (91.6%, down from 100%), St. Louis (23.1%, down from 27.1%), Austin (124.8%, down from 128.2%), Dallas (118.6%, down from 120.5%), Jacksonville, FL, Pittsburgh and Los Angeles. All of them remain buyer’s markets.

#110642. How an Artsy Pennsylvania River Town Became an Architectural Powerhouse Where Old Meets Upcoming

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1279 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Realtor ↗ Open Full Page

How an Artsy Pennsylvania River Town Became an Architectural Powerhouse Where Old Meets Upcoming

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1279 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtor

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that at first glance, New Hope, PA, looks like little more than a picturesque, upscale river town with a vibrant arts scene.
  • It has been revealed that located halfway between New York City and Philadelphia, New Hope spans roughly 1.42 square miles and is home to fewer than 3,000 year-round residents.
  • In Fresh Hope's luxury housing market, old and new blend seamlessly: 18th-century structures are brought into the 21st century with bold, modern additions and amenities.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that at first glance, New Hope, PA, looks like little more than a picturesque, upscale river town with a vibrant arts scene. However, a closer look reveals that the historic borough shares an architectural DNA with Europe's premier capitals.

It has been revealed that located halfway between New York City and Philadelphia, New Hope spans roughly 1.42 square miles and is home to fewer than 3,000 year-round residents. Yet it boasts an outsized reputation as a beloved regional tourist destination renowned for its art galleries, boutiques, riverside dining, and cultural institutions, led by the iconic Bucks County Playhouse, which has hosted major stars such as Grace Kelly, Robert Redford, and Liza Minnelli.

In Fresh Hope's luxury housing market, old and new blend seamlessly: 18th-century structures are brought into the 21st century with bold, modern additions and amenities.

"A lot of the homes around here, especially some of the larger homes, all started off as an old stone farmhouse, so incorporating some of that character while building the significant steel and glass additions is very much an architectural vibe that is done here," Nicholas Esser, managing partner at Addison Wolfe Real Estate, tells Realtor.com®.

The market's remarkably varied housing stock also includes stately Colonial and Victorian homes, sprawling legacy estates, and cutting-edge newly introduced construction that would not look out of place in the heart of Silicon Valley.

Architect Ralph Fey, with Ralph C. Fey Architects in Doylestown, PA, explains that New Hope's signature look is rooted in regulatory necessity, because more than half of the town falls in a strictly regulated historic district, which rarely allows older buildings to be torn down to make way for new builds.

Rather than viewing zoning laws as a creative roadblock, Fey has made his professional mark by seamlessly merging history with contemporary living.

In a recent development, "Some of the best architecture is born out of constraints," he tells Realtor.com. "The goal, the fun, the challenge is how to maintain that historic feel, meet the guidelines of the historic district, but provide the amenities that we now want to have as we live on the water.".

Maureen Reynolds, a Serhant luxury real estate agent in Fresh Hope, counts herself among Fey's clients. She at the moment lives in an 1832-built converted horse barn with tall ceilings and hand-hewn beams.

"I have all the modern amenities because of Ralph," she tells Realtor.com.

While Newly introduced Hope lacks the urban density and wealth of major metros, Fey indicates, its architectural style "is more like London, where you have newer construction next to historic construction, next to really historic construction, and it is that fabric that makes London so exciting.".

Founded in the 18th century on the banks of the Delaware River, Upcoming Hope was previously called Wells Ferry and later Coryell’s Ferry.

Industry observers note that the borough was rechristened after a fire in 1790 destroyed several mills owned by local businessman Benjamin Parry. He rebuilt them as the New Hope Mills, inspiring the town’s optimistic new name.

By the late 19th century, Newly introduced Hope had gained a reputation as an art colony and emerged as a major hub for American and Pennsylvania Impressionists, including William Langson Lathrop, Edward Willis Redfield, and Daniel Garber.

It has been revealed that "Latest Hope definitely has an architectural richness that's been developed over centuries," notes Reynolds. "Its historic buildings' relationship to the river and surrounding landscape give it a character that cannot be created overnight. And the challenge and opportunity for the architects, for Realtors®, and for developers is to respect that history while designing homes that accommodate the way people live today.".

Fey agrees, maintaining that Fresh Hope's success as a thriving housing market is rooted in its past and the borough's fierce commitment to protecting it.

According to recent reports, "The same little river town 5 miles down the road that did not have a historic district, where all the homes were knocked down, would not have that feel of a classic historic town, and would not have that charm, and it could potentially lose it," he indicates. "It's really important to us as architects to preserve that feeling, and that's part of the reason why Fresh Hope is as prized and treasured as it is—it's for its history.".

Even with fresh construction, a premium is placed on designing in harmony with the town.

Fey and Reynolds frequently work with clients to select natural building materials such as locally sourced stone, cedar wood, and slate roof tiles. They complement surrounding centuries-old structures rather than clashing with the local aesthetic.

"Most of my clients are very in love with the feel of the historic Upcoming Hope and also would like to see some of the amenities of slightly more glass, slightly higher ceilings," notes the architect. "So when we are doing additions on the traditional homes or existing historic housing stock, our goal is to contribute to the street.".

It has been revealed that despite its modest size, Upcoming Hope commands an impressively broad appeal. Esser and Fey say buyers range from locals looking to upgrade or build their dream homes to affluent transplants from neighboring New York, Philadelphia, and New Jersey hunting for a primary residence or weekend pied-à-terre, alongside retirees drawn to Pennsylvania's favorable tax climate.

Some home shoppers, however, come from much farther afield.

Reynolds’ roster of New Hope clients includes buyers from the South of France, Sweden, Canada, and Japan, cementing the town’s status as a market punching well above its weight.

In August, the Philadelphia Business Journal ranked New Hope as the nation's No. 2 hottest luxury housing market during the second quarter of 2026 among 327 markets analyzed.

"That's an extraordinary distinction for a community of this size," notes Reynolds.

It has been revealed that prices have surged accordingly. Reynolds recounts how townhomes originally priced between $1.4 million and $1.8 million jumped to $2 million–$3.2 million in less than three years.

The latest Realtor.com housing data shows that in October, the median listing price in New Hope topped $2 million, up more than 27% from a year ago.

Meanwhile, the luxury-tier threshold—representing the top 10% of the market—was just over $5 million.

While inventory was up more than 50% year over year last month, Realtor.com senior economist Hannah Jones notes that supply still remains nearly 60% below pre-pandemic levels.

“Demand comes largely from cash-rich buyers in the surrounding region, including a growing share from Fresh Jersey alongside the New York metro, who are insulated from mortgage rates hovering around 7%,” she notes.

As always with real estate, location remains paramount.

"If I have something on the river, it usually sells within a couple days, and that can be something, too, that is not turnkey—we're talking about something that can be slightly a shell inside," notes Reynolds.

Ultimately, what keeps buyers flocking to New Hope from near and far is the sheer architectural variety packed into the pint-sized, picture-perfect historic borough.

"The beautiful thing around here is that there's gorgeous properties everywhere, and the home styles do change between the more modern construction, with the beams and 12-foot ceilings, and old stone construction, but they mesh really well," concludes Esser.

In a recent development, snejana Farberov is a reporter at Realtor.com covering the U.S. housing market and the latest domestic real estate trends. She has worked as a general assignment journalist in Latest York City and Long Island for 16 years, writing for New York Post, Daily Mail, and News 12. It has been revealed that in 2022, Buterin argued for a land value tax. According to him, such a tax would lower the upfront cost of buying a home and discourage speculation on vacant lots.

In 2025, the Ethereum co-founder called the housing market a "confusing market of peculiar NFTs." According to Buterin, what is really being sold under the label of square footage is the right to live in a particular city. Industry observers note that MEXC confirmed that its Global Card service will be discontinued on November 18, according to the exchange's announcement. The organization cites service adjustments by its third-party card issuer. From the deadline, existing cards can no longer be used for transactions, and upcoming card applications are suspended.

Users have two things to take care of before the service ends.

First, the remaining card balance has to be withdrawn: the Withdraw button on the Global Card page sends the funds to the Fiat account.

Recent findings suggest that second, subscriptions linked to the card should be cancelled or switched to another payment method. Unfortunately for cardholders, recurring payments will most likely fail if they stay on the old card.

Sources indicate that if there's still a balance when the service ends, MEXC will credit it to the Spot account, so people will simply receive their funds back. It's notable to keep in mind that pending card transactions need time to settle, which is why the balance snapshot comes on November 21, three days after the shutdown. The amount will be credited within three business days of the snapshot. Users do not need to take any action.

Industry observers note that refunds for previous card transactions will be credited to the Fiat account once MEXC receives them. Pending cashback will be credited automatically as scheduled. Elite VVIP users with zero-fee benefits will be refunded too, though the eligible fees return to their Spot accounts only before December 15.

Transaction history, card orders and cashback records stay available on the Global Card page for three months after the service ends, so it's worth saving anything needed before access ends.

Cryptocurrency services delegate certain types of services to third parties all the time, so witnessing a similar situation is more than a possibility here. Realistically, the shutdown is somewhat inconvenient rather than dangerous, as the balances are returned automatically. For consumers: stay vigilant and try not to put all your eggs in one basket.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

California-born sculptor Chester Beach worked out of a Latest York City studio between 1907 and 1952, nabbing high-profile commissions from the Panama-Pacific International Exposition, as well as the 1928 Summer Olympics.

But, like many artists, he carved out space for a pastoral retreat away from the hustle and bustle.

Industry observers note that in 1917, after living in Rome for a brief period, he and his wife, Eleanor Beach, established a home in Brewster, NY, in Putnam County, just 55 miles north of the city. They named the Arts & Crafts-style estate OldWalls.

Now these 10.49 acres—including four buildings, comprising a compound—is looking for a fresh steward.

"There have only been three owners including the original family that owned it up until 2009," says listing agent Will Stuart, of Berkshire Hathaway HomeServices Latest England Properties. "My sellers have been there for two years.".

Listing for $4,150,000, the new owner won't be the first to seek a deeper connection to nature while still being close to Manhattan.

Stuart notes that this eight-bedroom, 6.5-bath spread is exceptionally tied to its origins.

"Each owner has become a steward of the property and has preserved extensive family photographs, memoirs and documents, and have really kept the story going, which is rare with these kinds of properties," he claims. "A lot of times the information gets lost along the way. The story has been preserved so well.".

Sources indicate that the estate includes a four-bedroom stone residence with plaster walls, hand-crafted stonework and stained glass. There’s also a separate guest studio with a kitchen, bath, sleeping loft and stone fireplace. And, a two-bedroom guest cottage dating back to the 1940s with cozy amenities such as a fireplace and screened-in porch.

Another way the property has been preserved is through art the original owners brought into the house.

It has been revealed that tiles collected from Spain, Guatemala and Italy are laid into the floor, indicates Stuart. He adds that "there’s actually a cluster of Roman floor tiles under the dining-room table.".

The kitchen’s chandelier was born out of a turntable Beach used for sculpting. Eleanor’s bird paintings (112 in all) are incorporated into the living room’s ceiling.

According to recent reports, “There’s three outbuildings in addition to the main residence that all offer incredible living space and charm,” says Stuart. “Each one of them has a story and a history.”.

For example, in the detached studio, which was built before the home, are many of Beach’s tools and hardware, as well as the original doors.

In a recent development, A buyer drawn to that history is who Stuart is courting. But it could also be an equestrian, as the property features a five-stall barn with a spacious one-bedroom apartment. Nearby are run-outs, rolling grass turnout paddocks, a riding field with access to trails, and a riding arena in the sand.

In a recent development, “We have a lot of equestrians that have moved into the community,” says Stuart. “A lot of the equestrian people travel to Florida in the winter so they’re here half the year, but most people are here year-round.” Two miles down the road is Old Salem Farm, a 120-acre boarding and training facility.

Above all, the buyer will likely be someone who likes to be near Manhattan but also have a countryside retreat, just like Beach once did.

According to recent reports, this mirrors a trend Stuart continues to see among buyers. “People looking for more space, more privacy, but want to stay within close proximity to the city,” he says. “This is a real compound here. It’s someone who is hosting family or guests.”.

Brokerage expansion stretched from the Caribbean to the West Coast in recent days, as firms moved into latest markets and picked up agents and teams from other companies. Engel & Völkers is headed to Aruba, where it plans to open a shop in April 2027, and Realty of America reached California with Zandra Ulloa and 12 of her Team Z Realty agents in San Diego.

eXp Realty picked up a Tampa Bay brokerage and a Cincinnati-area team that spent 20 years with REMAX. Baird & Warner brought on Oak Park, Illinois, boutique Beyond Properties, and Dane Briggs teamed up with Phil Sexton at HomeSmart’s NEXT team. The shop is projected to open in April 2027 at L.G. Smith Blvd. 330 in Palm Beach and will serve clients across the island, according to the manufacturer.

“Aruba is a compelling addition to the network’s growing presence in the Caribbean,” Stuart Siegel, president and CEO of Engel & Völkers Americas, stated in a statement.

Recent findings suggest that realty of America entered California with Zandra Ulloa and 12 Team Z Realty agent partners in San Diego. Ulloa has generated more than $4.2 billion in sales volume over her 13-year career, and Team Z peaked at 72 agents and $589 million in annual volume, according to the company. Agent-owned ROA, founded in September 2024, indicates it has more than 3,900 agents across 26 markets.

“People around me may see what I am giving up, but I see what I am making room for,” Ulloa remarked in a statement.

Rene Carpena and Dana Carpena moved Florida’s 1st Choice Realty, their independent Greater Tampa Bay brokerage, to eXp Realty, where it now operates as 1st Choice Collective. The group brings more than 70 agents and support staff and recorded more than 325 transactions and $60 million in sales volume in 2025, according to the company.

In a recent development, jon Bowling also brought his 17-person team in Mason, Ohio, to eXp after 20 years with RE/MAX. eXp Realty is the core subsidiary of AGNT Inc.

It has been revealed that baird & Warner added Beyond Properties, a boutique brokerage in Oak Park, Illinois, whose dozen agents will operate as Beyond Properties Group. Owner and designated managing broker Erica Cuneen, who founded the firm almost 20 years ago, will co-lead the group with team leader Cynthia Howe Gajewski. The group joins Baird & Warner’s Oak Park office and keeps its Marion Street location.

“This partnership will allow me to simplify the operational side of the business and spend more time doing what I love, which is focusing on our agents and clients,” Cuneen said in a statement.

Dane Briggs, an Arizona real estate veteran, partnered with Phil Sexton, founder of HomeSmart’s NEXT team, in a leadership role focused on agent workflows and AI integrations. Briggs has worked as a designated broker and title executive, founded referral brokerage Roosted and led expansion initiatives at Homie. He has also served as an Inman Ambassador.

Sources indicate that “Before long, we weren’t just talking about what Phil was building. We were talking about what we could build together,” Briggs remarked in a statement.

According to recent reports, IRES MLS, which serves Northern Colorado and parts of the Front Range, rehired Samantha Ewing as director of operations. Ewing spent 13 years at IRES as a projects manager and quality assurance tester before leaving in 2018, and she has more than 20 years of experience in MLS operations and real estate technology.

“Having Samantha return to IRES is an exciting opportunity for our team and the local industry we serve,” CEO Julie Dahl said in a statement.

Howard Hanna Portside Real Estate Group added Melissa Winter, an agent with nearly 15 years of experience who focuses on first-time homebuyers, to its Massachusetts team in Amesbury. Portside, which has more than 200 agents, entered a strategic partnership with Howard Hanna in 2026, according to the company.

“What drew me to Portside was the energy, the people, and the opportunity for growth,” Winter stated in a statement.

Cardano-based stablecoin DJED has announced its sunset, as DJED and SHEN services will wind down on December 31, 2026, at 11:59 pm UTC.

DJED represents a crypto-backed, overcollateralized stablecoin protocol on Cardano whose US-dollar peg is maintained algorithmically against an ADA reserve (with SHEN as the reserve coin), rather than by fiat reserves.

"DJED and SHEN services will wind down at the end of December 31, 2026, at 11:59 pm UTC," a DJED-focused X account wrote.

According to recent reports, ATTN: DJED & SHEN Holders DJED and SHEN services will wind down at the end of December 31, 2026 at 11:59pm UTC. Please redeem and convert any DJED and SHEN you hold before then. All redemptions are subject to the reserve ratio.

Recent findings suggest that consumers are urged to redeem and convert any DJED and SHEN they hold before this deadline. Users are to redeem on the protocol and convert their DJED and SHEN back to ADA on the official Djed page. Users who hold DJED or SHEN in liquidity pools, lending markets, or other DeFi platforms are urged to withdraw those positions first, then redeem or swap.

The Djed team noted all systems are fully operational and redemptions are now open, subject to the reserve ratio. It further added that the Djed protocol will be maintained and remain available until December 31, 2026. After this date, all remaining funds will be allocated to the outstanding DJED/SHEN holders once the wind-down is complete.

Djed’s shutdown comes almost three years after its launch, which came in 2023. The stablecoin was officially debuted on the Cardano mainnet on January 31, 2023, and was developed by COTI in collaboration with the Cardano ecosystem to be used on DeFi protocols on Cardano as a stable alternative to volatile cryptocurrencies.

In positive news for the Cardano ecosystem, Monument Bank Limited has released tokenized deposits on the Midnight network, marking a milestone for the network and the decentralized finance ecosystem.

At present, Monument is the first UK bank to tokenize retail deposits on a public blockchain, offering clients a 5.2% AER fixed-term return on savings directly through its existing banking app, delivering institutional onchain finance through a familiar and user-friendly banking experience.

Up to £250 million of client deposits will be represented on Midnight in this opening phase, with deposits recorded one-to-one in sterling.

Ahmed Barakat is a journalist and copywriter based in Georgia with a growing focus on blockchain technology, DeFi, AI, privacy, digital assets, and fintech innovation.

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Privacy coins are poised to be among the biggest cryptocurrency stories of 2027, driven by growing concerns over financial surveillance, institutional adoption, and the future of digital privacy. This creates a compelling investment narrative. Google Gemini AI predicts that two projects, Monero (XMR) and Zcash (ZEC), will stand out, and it aims to forecast which will experience a significant price surge in 2027.

Both Monero and Zcash are established leaders in the privacy-focused cryptocurrency space, but they employ fundamentally different approaches to protecting users’ financial information. Monero offers privacy by default, while Zcash seeks to balance financial confidentiality with greater accessibility for institutional investors.

As a potential major crypto bull market approaches in 2027, investors may find two distinct opportunities for substantial returns. However, determining which option could deliver the biggest gains may yield surprising results.

It has been revealed that monero has long been considered the gold standard for transaction privacy. Unlike conventional cryptocurrencies, where transactions can be publicly inspected on a blockchain, XMR makes privacy an inherent feature of its network.

In a recent development, it achieves this through ring signatures, Ring Confidential Transactions (RingCT), and stealth addresses, which conceal the sender, transaction amount, and recipient. Importantly, privacy is mandatory, not optional.

This gives Monero a compelling proposition as a digital cash alternative, especially as blockchain analytics grow more sophisticated and financial surveillance expands.

In a recent development, however, that same characteristic creates a significant obstacle: regulatory scrutiny. Exchanges in several jurisdictions have restricted or removed XMR trading, potentially limiting access to a broader pool of investors.

Zcash takes a different approach, using zero-knowledge cryptography to enable shielded transactions while retaining the option of transparent transactions.

According to recent reports, its shielded addresses let owners conceal transaction details, while viewing keys let them selectively disclose information to auditors or other authorized parties. This flexibility could prove particularly attractive to institutions that want privacy without completely sacrificing compliance.

The distinction could become increasingly important as institutional investors look beyond Bitcoin and Ethereum for opportunities in specialized crypto sectors.

Recent findings suggest that privacy coins are already attracting attention beyond their traditional communities. Zcash has made considerable progress in positioning itself as a more institutionally accessible privacy network, with regulated investment products emerging and interest in its underlying technology growing.

Meanwhile, Monero continues to benefit from its established reputation, consistent privacy guarantees and decentralized architecture.

In a recent development, the broader investment narrative is also changing. As cryptocurrency adoption increases, more transactions become visible to blockchain analytics companies, incentivizing individuals and businesses to seek greater financial confidentiality.

In a recent development, however, the regulatory landscape could become a major obstacle in 2027. The EU’s Anti-Money Laundering Regulation is scheduled to apply from July 10, 2027, with restrictions covering crypto-asset accounts involving anonymity-enhancing coins.

Recent findings suggest that crucially, the legislation’s definition encompasses privacy features that operate either systematically or optionally. This means neither project can assume its architecture provides an exemption.

Looking beyond daily price fluctuations, the weekly and monthly charts will be particularly important in determining which cryptocurrency has the strongest potential heading into 2027.

For Monero, the key technical consideration is whether it can establish a sustained higher-high structure following its previous major market cycle. A successful retest of former resistance zones as support could lay the groundwork for another substantial move, particularly if capital rotates toward privacy-focused assets.

XMR also benefits from a relatively predictable supply model. Its permanent tail emission produces 0.6 XMR every two minutes, with an inflation rate that gradually declines over time.

Zcash, meanwhile, has a more conventional fixed supply of 21 million coins, giving it a familiar scarcity narrative. Its longer-term technical outlook will depend heavily on whether it can maintain gains tied to its growing institutional profile and establish stronger historical support.

Both could benefit enormously from a broader cryptocurrency bull market, although ZEC’s previous outperformance means investors should also consider the possibility of profit-taking and deeper corrections.

There are compelling arguments for both projects, but their potential price trajectories could look quite different. In an optimistic 2027 scenario, Zcash could target a broad trading range of $1,600–$2,400, supported by institutional demand, increased shielded transaction adoption, and a stronger position within the privacy sector.

Monero could potentially push towards $900–$1,400, with a particularly bullish scenario opening the door to even higher valuations if demand for censorship-resistant digital cash accelerates.

Recent findings suggest that these are speculative price scenarios, not technical guarantees, and regulatory restrictions remain a substantial risk for both projects. Nevertheless, one notable consideration could give XMR the advantage: its established position as a dedicated privacy currency.

Zcash arguably has the stronger institutional narrative, but Monero arguably has the stronger proposition for consumers who consider financial privacy non-negotiable. If that distinction becomes increasingly vital during the next market cycle, demand for XMR could accelerate considerably.

While Zcash could continue attracting institutional capital and potentially deliver impressive returns, I believe Monero has the ingredients for a stronger percentage gain over the longer term.

Its established reputation, mandatory privacy architecture, and potential to benefit from renewed demand for financial anonymity make it an intriguing candidate. If privacy becomes one of crypto’s defining investment narratives in 2027, XMR could be one of the biggest beneficiaries.

Sources indicate that to leave, participants must voluntarily withdraw, be medically withdrawn by a DS (directing staff) due to injury or be dismissed for refusing a direct order. During the final test, the DS ejects those who fail the interrogation or selection test.

Season 5 is set in the Malaysian jungle. It features Candace Cameron Bure, Brandi Glanville, Oliver Hudson, Ruby Rose, George Santos, Bre Tiesi, Matt Barnes, and Mauricio and Alexia Umansky, among others.

At the time that this article was published, Alexia was still in the competition. Mauricio voluntarily withdrew after a rib injury sustained during a hand-to-hand fighting challenge with former NBA player Matt Barnes. Mauricio mentioned the injury took two or three months to heal.

Inman spoke to Mauricio and Alexia midway through the season about the experience, the latest industry news and what’s next for The Agency.

Tech Report: Inference pushes AI to smaller sites, making the data layer the deciding factor

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that inference is moving to the center of enterprise AI spending, and the AI data layer is emerging as the piece that decides whether those investments pay off.
  • That shift is putting storage companies with roots in high-performance computing at the center of the AI conversation.
  • According to recent reports, “As inference is off the charts in terms of utilization, the data layer is what makes a difference,” Bouzari said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 15:09 EST / NOVEMBER 20 2026.

Recent findings suggest that inference is moving to the center of enterprise AI spending, and the AI data layer is emerging as the piece that decides whether those investments pay off. As GPU costs climb and component shortages persist, the architecture behind AI is shifting from a handful of massive facilities toward a distributed web of smaller sites.

That shift is putting storage companies with roots in high-performance computing at the center of the AI conversation. Turning data into insight at an acceptable cost now depends on a resilient, secure data engine built for GPU efficiency, according to Alex Bouzari (pictured), co-founder and chief executive officer of DataDirect Networks Inc.

According to recent reports, “As inference is off the charts in terms of utilization, the data layer is what makes a difference,” Bouzari said. “Costs are skyrocketing. GPUs are becoming more and more powerful, but also more and more expensive.”.

Bouzari spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how inference, cost pressure and shortages are reshaping AI infrastructure. (* Disclosure below.).

It has been revealed that the first wave of AI buildouts concentrated GPUs in large, power-hungry facilities. Inference changes that math because it needs to run close to people and their data, Bouzari explained. Communities are also pushing back on giant monolithic data centers, he added.

Industry observers note that “Now, what is happening with inference, you need to supplement that with smaller footprints. Let’s call them data centers, 1 megawatt, 2 megawatt, 5 megawatts. And those need to reside where the action is taking place, where the autonomous driving is happening, where physical AI is happening, where the sensor data is,” Bouzari noted.

Connecting small pods back to large AI factories requires a different approach to data. DDN is building a software layer that spans many types of hardware, a direction reflected in its recent move to free its EXAScaler file system from DDN’s own hardware. The goal is to squeeze more use out of very expensive gear, according to Bouzari.

“It is a software layer that needs to accommodate the different types of hardware because, look, the costs being so high, people want to be able to maximize the utilization over an extended period of time, just like it was in high-performance computing,” Bouzari stated.

The scale of spending has changed dramatically. A couple hundred million dollars once funded the world’s fastest supercomputer but now buys 15 to 20 racks of equipment, Bouzari noted. Shortages of GPUs, memory and solid-state drives are colliding with tighter budget scrutiny.

Sources indicate that “On the one hand, you have budgetary constraints and the need to extract as much value as you can from your investment,” Bouzari said. “On the other hand, you have the shortages. And so a data layer that can do a lot more with a lot less infrastructure, the smaller footprint is extremely valuable.”.

That thinking extends into the enterprise. DDN’s Enterprise AI HyperPOD packages CPUs, GPUs, networking and storage into a rack that can drop into existing corporate sites with available power. Keeping the pod on-premises also gives companies tighter control over their data, Bouzari explained.

“I think we’re entering an era where we will see a blossoming of smaller footprint pods being deployed in enterprises globally,” Bouzari said.

Bouzari framed the AI data layer as the counterpart to accelerated compute, with Nvidia Corp. supplying the processing and DDN supplying the data. As inference and agents take over, the data side carries more weight, he mentioned: “You need both to make it successful. But the data engine, I think, is becoming increasingly key as inference and agentic is really becoming the predominant way to utilize AI and get value out of it.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just a week after Binance suffered the biggest cyberattack seen in the history of the crypto market, the onchain monitoring platform Whale Alert has spotted the hacker moving some of the funds in large quantities.

The transfer has raised concerns across the crypto community about what the hacker might be up to and about the possibility of Binance recovering the stolen funds, especially after they are moved to another wallet.

Although the source did not provide sufficient details about the highly concerning transfer, it highlighted that the attacker behind the 2026 Binance hack moved 60,000 ETH on Wednesday in 2026.

The broader crypto market has continued to suffer extreme volatility since the attack happened in late October. Hence, the total portion of Ethereum tokens transferred from the stolen stash is now worth $108.78 million at ETH’s current market price.

While the reason behind the sudden move after a few weeks of silence remains uncertain, further data showed that the assets were moved in five separate transfers of 12,000 ETH each.

Notably, each transaction was worth between $21.75 million and $21.77 million, and they were identified as Binance’s stolen funds because they were all moved from a wallet labeled 'Binance hack' in 2026.

Considering the history of the transferred funds, the move has sparked speculation that the hacker might already be preparing to spend the stolen funds, further sabotaging Binance’s chances of full recovery.

However, it is important to note that there is no evidence that the attacker has sold the Ethereum, as the receiving wallet has not been identified.
